page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-24 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the GPU Machines family. The instance is built on an x86_64 architecture and provides 24 dedicated vCPUs alongside 90.0 GB of system RAM, resulting in an allocation of 3.75 GB of memory per core. Compute resources are paired with a fractional NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 accelerator, providing 0.5 of a physical GPU and 48 GB of total GPU video memory (VRAM).

Regarding physical layout and input/output capabilities, the instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for disk operations and root filesystems. External networking configurations do not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating Cloud NAT or reserved external IPs for internet egress. The hardware partitioning provides a cost-effective point of entry into NVIDIA Blackwell architecture by offering fractional GPU resources, eliminating the overhead of reserving a full discrete graphics card for tasks that do not require full GPU allocation.

The combination of 24 dedicated vCPUs, 48 GB of GPU memory, and 90 GB of host RAM makes the g4-standard-24 suited for graphic-intensive workloads, remote visualization, computer-aided design (CAD), digital content creation, and moderate machine learning inference pipelines. Workloads relying on significant local I/O performance will face architectural tradeoffs due to the absence of integrated local storage.

The instance includes no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached storage options, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By allocating a fractional GPU, the server presents a balanced hardware profile that avoids the cost overhead of a fully dedicated accelerator while maintaining substantial video memory. This configuration is aligned with graphic rendering, remote visualization, CAD applications, and medium-scale AI inference workloads.
